'''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Tumulus (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped burial mound|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Burial Mound Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped burial mound|ja|前方後円墳}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped burial mound || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round burial mound|ja|円墳}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of burial mounds, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items).
