Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | group = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! Shape !! Size !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-scale tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-typed keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-typed Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-typed Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important other_designation of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == Burial Facility == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === Important other_designation (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important other_designation Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as Important other_designation of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === Important other_designation (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and Important other_designation Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | part_of = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! type !! area !! Constructed !! Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Historic Site Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:01, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | part_of = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Constructed !! other_designation Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items).
