Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | part_of = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | latitude = 36|longitude = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | artifacts = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = Artifacts designated as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | icon = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! type !! area !! Constructed !! other_designation Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. Artifacts excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * Artifacts excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun Artifacts}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's dimensions are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | part_of = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | coordinates = 36|coordinates = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | size = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = burial goods designation1 as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | label = Kabutozuka Kofun | type = | label_position = top }} == Overview ==

Constructed !! other_designation Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_other_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_other_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Constructed !! other_designation Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | part_of = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | coordinates = 36|coordinates = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | area = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = burial goods other_designation1 as Important Cultural Property of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | map_dot_label = Kabutozuka Kofun | type = | map_dot_label = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! type !! area !! Constructed !! other_designation Status |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] Designation] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National Cultural Property Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National other_designation |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National other_designation |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural other_designation |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural other_designation |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary other_designation): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintother_designation Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were other_designation1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == other_designation == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' (甲塚古墳) {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} | name = Kabutozuka Kofun | image = [[File:Kabutozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke) zenkei.JPG|280px]]
Kofun (central posterior mound, left anterior mound) | part_of = Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) | location = {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, Tochigi Prefecture, Kokubunji 847 | coordinates = 36|coordinates = 139|latd = 36|latm = 23|lats = 1.80|longd = 139|longm = 48|longs = 18.15 | iso = JP-09 | type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} | area = Mound length: 80m | constructed = Late 6th century | burial facility = {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} | deceased = Unknown | burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}}, {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}}, {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} | historic site = None | cultural property = burial goods Historic Site1 as Important designation1 of Japan | map = Japan Tochigi | map_dot_label = Kabutozuka Kofun | type = | map_dot_label = top }} == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! type !! area !! Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items).
