Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+Shimotsuke Kofun Cluster (Iizuka-Kokubunji Area) Summary ! name !! type !! area !! Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). 分布図}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1= {{Coord|36|22|20.39|N|139|48|21.31|E}} | label1=摩利支天塚 | label-pos1=right | label-color1=black | mark1=前方後円墳-南西.png | mark-size1=30 | mark-coord2= {{Coord|36|22|30.88|N|139|48|25.67|E}} | label2=琵琶塚 | label-pos2=right | label-color2=black | mark2=前方後円墳-南西.png | mark-size2=30 | mark-coord3= {{Coord|36|24|15.15|N|139|48|41.13|E}} | label3=吾妻 | label-pos3=right | label-color3=black | mark3=前方後円墳-南南東.png | mark-size3=30 | mark-coord4= {{Coord|36|23|1.80|N|139|48|18.15|E}} | label4=甲塚 | label-pos4=left | label-color4=black | mark4=帆立貝形古墳-南.png | mark-size4=25 | mark-coord5= {{Coord|36|23|33.06|N|139|48|23.26|E}} | label5=愛宕塚 | label-pos5=left | label-color5=black | mark5=前方後円墳-西南西.png | mark-size5=25 | mark-coord6= {{Coord|36|23|38.85|N|139|48|34.73|E}} | label6=山王塚 | label-pos6=left | label-color6=black | mark6=前方後円墳-西.png | mark-size6=25 | mark-coord7= {{Coord|36|23|41.67|N|139|48|39.60|E}} | label7=丸塚 | label-pos7=right | label-color7=black | mark7=円墳.png | mark-size7=25 | mark-coord8= {{Coord|36|23|6.21|N|139|48|21.95|E}} | label8=下野国分寺跡 | label-pos8=top | label-color8=black | mark8=Red pog.svg | mark-size8=10 | mark-coord9= {{Coord|36|23|6.98|N|139|48|44.73|E}} | label9=下野国分尼寺跡 | label-pos9=right | label-color9=black | mark9=Red pog.svg | mark-size9=10 | mark-coord10= {{Coord|36|22|47.5|N|139|47|6.3|E}} | label10=下野国庁跡 | label-pos10=right | label-color10=black | mark10=Red pog.svg | mark-size10=10 }} '''甲塚古墳'''（かぶとづかこふん）は、[[栃木県]][[下野市]]国分寺にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[帆立貝形古墳]]。しもつけ古墳群（うち飯塚・国分寺地域）を構成する古墳の1つ。史跡指定はされていない[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 甲塚古墳]（下野市文化財バーチャルミュージアム）。。出土品は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+しもつけ古墳群（飯塚・国分寺地域）一覧 !古墳名!!形状!!規模!!築造時期!!史跡指定 |- |[[摩利支天塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||墳丘長120m||5c末||国史跡 |- |[[琵琶塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長123m||6c初頭||国史跡 |- |[[吾妻古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長128m||6c後半||国史跡 |- |'''甲塚古墳'''||[[帆立貝形古墳]]||墳丘長80m||6c後半||なし |- |[[愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|愛宕塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長78.5m||6c末||県史跡 |- |[[山王塚古墳 (下野市)|山王塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長89m||6c末-7c初頭||なし |- |[[丸塚古墳 (下野市)|丸塚古墳]]||[[円墳]]||直径65m||7c前半||県史跡 |}
[[ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|埴輪群（国の[[重要文化財]]）}}{{small|しもつけ風土記の丘資料館展示（他画像も同様）。}}]] 栃木県南部、[[下野市]]西部の[[姿川]]と[[思川 (栃木県)|思川]]に挟まれた台地上に築造された古墳である。台地上では、本古墳のほかにも[[摩利支天塚古墳]]・[[琵琶塚古墳]]・[[吾妻古墳]]を始めとする大型古墳の分布が知られる。本古墳では[[1883年|1883]]・[[1893年]]（[[明治]]16・26年）に発掘がなされ旧状が損なわれているほか、考古学的にはこれまでに数次の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳丘は前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南方向に向ける史跡説明板。。墳丘は2段築成で、特に1段目は平坦な基壇状を呈し、下野地域特有の「下野型古墳」の特徴を示す。墳丘長は推定約80メートル、主丘（ほぼ完全な円形）は直径61メートルを測る。墳丘第1段の平坦面中央部には[[円筒埴輪]]列が巡らされる。また第2段のくびれ部付近において[[形象埴輪]]（人物形・馬形埴輪など）が検出されており、特に埴輪群は当初の位置・向きまで良好に遺存する点、全国初の機織形埴輪の出土の点、一部の埴輪に彩色の残る点で注目される{{Sfn|甲塚古墳出土埴輪（下野市）}}読売新聞栃木版 2017年8月14日 20面。。埋葬施設は[[凝灰岩]]製の[[横穴式石室]]で、前方部前面において南方向に開口する。築造時期は[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃と推定される。 出土品は[[2017年]]（[[平成]]29年）に国の[[重要文化財]]に指定された。付近では、後世に[[下野国分寺跡|下野国分寺]]が隣接して営まれている。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては[[凝灰岩]]製切石による[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、前方部前面において南方向に開口する。現在までに損壊を受けているが、推定復原される石室の規模は次の通り。 * 石室全長：4.2メートル - 墓道を含めると約9メートル。 * 玄室：長さ3.0メートル、幅2.0メートル、高さ1.9メートル * 羨道：長さ0.6メートル == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 栃木県甲塚古墳出土品（考古資料） - 明細は以下。下野市立しもつけ風土記の丘資料館保管。2017年（平成29年）9月15日指定平成29年9月15日文部科学省告示第117号。[https://web.archive.org/web/20170310112148/http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html 国宝・重要文化財の指定について]（文化庁）。{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|00011756|栃木県甲塚古墳出土品}}。 ** 機織形埴輪 2点 ** 人物埴輪 17点 ** 馬形埴輪 4点 ** 須恵器 58点 ** 土師器 16点 ** （附指定）埴輪残欠 4点 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 機織形埴輪.JPG|機織形埴輪 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪1 (女性).JPG|人物埴輪1（女性） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪2 (女性).JPG|人物埴輪2（女性） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪15 (男性).JPG|人物埴輪15（男性） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪 (盾持人).JPG|人物埴輪（盾持人） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 馬形埴輪1.JPG|馬形埴輪1 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 馬形埴輪3.JPG|馬形埴輪3 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 土器群.JPG|土器群 == 関連施設 == * しもつけ風土記の丘資料館（下野市国分寺） - Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). 分布図}} | scalemark = 60 | mark-coord1= {{Coord|36|22|20.39|N|139|48|21.31|E}} | label1=摩利支天塚 | label-pos1=right | label-color1=black | mark1=前方後円墳-南西.png | mark-size1=30 | mark-coord2= {{Coord|36|22|30.88|N|139|48|25.67|E}} | label2=琵琶塚 | label-pos2=right | label-color2=black | mark2=前方後円墳-南西.png | mark-size2=30 | mark-coord3= {{Coord|36|24|15.15|N|139|48|41.13|E}} | label3=吾妻 | label-pos3=right | label-color3=black | mark3=前方後円墳-南南東.png | mark-size3=30 | mark-coord4= {{Coord|36|23|1.80|N|139|48|18.15|E}} | label4=甲塚 | label-pos4=left | label-color4=black | mark4=帆立貝形古墳-南.png | mark-size4=25 | mark-coord5= {{Coord|36|23|33.06|N|139|48|23.26|E}} | label5=愛宕塚 | label-pos5=left | label-color5=black | mark5=前方後円墳-西南西.png | mark-size5=25 | mark-coord6= {{Coord|36|23|38.85|N|139|48|34.73|E}} | label6=山王塚 | label-pos6=left | label-color6=black | mark6=前方後円墳-西.png | mark-size6=25 | mark-coord7= {{Coord|36|23|41.67|N|139|48|39.60|E}} | label7=丸塚 | label-pos7=right | label-color7=black | mark7=円墳.png | mark-size7=25 | mark-coord8= {{Coord|36|23|6.21|N|139|48|21.95|E}} | label8=下野国分寺跡 | label-pos8=top | label-color8=black | mark8=Red pog.svg | mark-size8=10 | mark-coord9= {{Coord|36|23|6.98|N|139|48|44.73|E}} | label9=下野国分尼寺跡 | label-pos9=right | label-color9=black | mark9=Red pog.svg | mark-size9=10 | mark-coord10= {{Coord|36|22|47.5|N|139|47|6.3|E}} | label10=下野国庁跡 | label-pos10=right | label-color10=black | mark10=Red pog.svg | mark-size10=10 }} '''甲塚古墳'''（かぶとづかこふん）は、[[栃木県]][[下野市]]国分寺にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[帆立貝形古墳]]。しもつけ古墳群（うち飯塚・国分寺地域）を構成する古墳の1つ。史跡指定はされていない[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 甲塚古墳]（下野市文化財バーチャルミュージアム）。。出土品は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている。 == 概要 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+しもつけ古墳群（飯塚・国分寺地域）一覧 !古墳名!!形状!!規模!!築造時期!!史跡指定 |- |[[摩利支天塚古墳]]||[[前方後円墳]]||墳丘長120m||5c末||国史跡 |- |[[琵琶塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長123m||6c初頭||国史跡 |- |[[吾妻古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長128m||6c後半||国史跡 |- |'''甲塚古墳'''||[[帆立貝形古墳]]||墳丘長80m||6c後半||なし |- |[[愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|愛宕塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長78.5m||6c末||県史跡 |- |[[山王塚古墳 (下野市)|山王塚古墳]]||前方後円墳||墳丘長89m||6c末-7c初頭||なし |- |[[丸塚古墳 (下野市)|丸塚古墳]]||[[円墳]]||直径65m||7c前半||県史跡 |}
[[ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 埴輪群.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|埴輪群（国の[[重要文化財]]）}}{{small|しもつけ風土記の丘資料館展示（他画像も同様）。}}]] 栃木県南部、[[下野市]]西部の[[姿川]]と[[思川 (栃木県)|思川]]に挟まれた台地上に築造された古墳である。台地上では、本古墳のほかにも[[摩利支天塚古墳]]・[[琵琶塚古墳]]・[[吾妻古墳]]を始めとする大型古墳の分布が知られる。本古墳では[[1883年|1883]]・[[1893年]]（[[明治]]16・26年）に発掘がなされ旧状が損なわれているほか、考古学的にはこれまでに数次の発掘調査が実施されている。 墳丘は前方部が短小な帆立貝形の前方後円形で、前方部を南方向に向ける史跡説明板。。墳丘は2段築成で、特に1段目は平坦な基壇状を呈し、下野地域特有の「下野型古墳」の特徴を示す。墳丘長は推定約80メートル、主丘（ほぼ完全な円形）は直径61メートルを測る。墳丘第1段の平坦面中央部には[[円筒埴輪]]列が巡らされる。また第2段のくびれ部付近において[[形象埴輪]]（人物形・馬形埴輪など）が検出されており、特に埴輪群は当初の位置・向きまで良好に遺存する点、全国初の機織形埴輪の出土の点、一部の埴輪に彩色の残る点で注目される{{Sfn|甲塚古墳出土埴輪（下野市）}}読売新聞栃木版 2017年8月14日 20面。。埋葬施設は[[凝灰岩]]製の[[横穴式石室]]で、前方部前面において南方向に開口する。築造時期は[[古墳時代]]後期の[[6世紀]]後半頃と推定される。 出土品は[[2017年]]（[[平成]]29年）に国の[[重要文化財]]に指定された。付近では、後世に[[下野国分寺跡|下野国分寺]]が隣接して営まれている。 == 埋葬施設 == 埋葬施設としては[[凝灰岩]]製切石による[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、前方部前面において南方向に開口する。現在までに損壊を受けているが、推定復原される石室の規模は次の通り。 * 石室全長：4.2メートル - 墓道を含めると約9メートル。 * 玄室：長さ3.0メートル、幅2.0メートル、高さ1.9メートル * 羨道：長さ0.6メートル == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 栃木県甲塚古墳出土品（考古資料） - 明細は以下。下野市立しもつけ風土記の丘資料館保管。2017年（平成29年）9月15日指定平成29年9月15日文部科学省告示第117号。[https://web.archive.org/web/20170310112148/http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html 国宝・重要文化財の指定について]（文化庁）。{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|00011756|栃木県甲塚古墳出土品}}。 ** 機織形埴輪 2点 ** 人物埴輪 17点 ** 馬形埴輪 4点 ** 須恵器 58点 ** 土師器 16点 ** （附指定）埴輪残欠 4点 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 機織形埴輪.JPG|機織形埴輪 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪1 (女性).JPG|人物埴輪1（女性） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪2 (女性).JPG|人物埴輪2（女性） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪15 (男性).JPG|人物埴輪15（男性） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 人物埴輪 (盾持人).JPG|人物埴輪（盾持人） ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 馬形埴輪1.JPG|馬形埴輪1 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 馬形埴輪3.JPG|馬形埴輪3 ファイル:甲塚古墳 (下野市) 出土 土器群.JPG|土器群 == 関連施設 == * しもつけ風土記の丘資料館（下野市国分寺） - 甲塚古墳出土品等を保管・展示。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用した文献）}} * 史跡説明板（下野市教育委員会設置） * {{Wikicite|reference={{PDFlink|[http://www.city.shimotsuke.lg.jp/manage/contents/upload/5821824673c0f.pdf 甲塚古墳出土埴輪]}}（下野市ホームページ）|ref={{Harvid|甲塚古墳出土埴輪（下野市）}}}} * {{Wikicite|reference={{PDFlink|[http://www.city.shimotsuke.lg.jp/manage/contents/upload/5821824666a85.pdf 甲塚古墳出土機織形埴輪]}}（下野市ホームページ）|ref={{Harvid|甲塚古墳出土機織形埴輪（下野市）}}}} == 関連文献 == {{small|（記事執筆に使用していない関連文献）}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2005|chapter=|title=甲塚古墳 栃木県国分寺町 平成16年度規模確認調査|publisher=栃木県国分寺町教育委員会|isbn=|page=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=とちぎ未来づくり財団埋蔵文化財センター|author=|year=2012|chapter=|title=甲塚古墳 重要遺跡範囲確認調査（栃木県埋蔵文化財調査報告 第343集）|publisher=栃木県教育委員会|isbn=|page=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2014|chapter=|title=甲塚古墳 下野国分寺跡史跡整備関連発掘調査報告書（下野市埋蔵文化財調査報告 第11集）|publisher=下野市教育委員会|isbn=|page=|ref=}} == 関連項目 == * [[下野国分寺跡]] == 外部リンク == * {{国指定文化財等データベース|201|00011756|栃木県甲塚古墳出土品}} * [http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 甲塚古墳]、[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=61 甲塚古墳出土遺物] - Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft|12=draft}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft|12=draft}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft|12=draft}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Constructed !! designation1 |- | {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || {{ill|Keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || Mound length: 120m || Late 5th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|| Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 123m || Early 6th century || National Historic Site |- | {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 128m || Late 6th century || National Historic Site |- | '''Kabutozuka Kofun''' || Scallop-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 80m || Late 6th century || None |- | {{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 78.5m || Late 6th century || Prefectural Historic Site |- | {{ill|Sannozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || Keyhole-shaped Kofun || Mound length: 89m || Late 6th–Early 7th century || None |- | {{ill|Marutsuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} || Diameter: 65m || Early 7th century || Prefectural Historic Site |}
Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|qq=}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke City|ja|下野市|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke City|qq=}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|qq=}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|qq=}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|ja|摩利支天塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Marishitenzuka Kofun|qq=}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|ja|琵琶塚古墳|1=Biwazuka Kofun|2=ja|3=琵琶塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Biwazuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Biwazuka Kofun|qq=}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|ja|吾妻古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Azuma Kofun|qq=}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniwa|qq=}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|qq=}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Sue pottery|qq=}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Haji pottery|qq=}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items).
