Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Omoi River (Tochigi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji Remains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. It is part of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja|しもつけ古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491515}} (Iizuka-Kokubunji area). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+List of Shimotsuke Kofuns (Iizuka-Kokubunji area) !Mound name!!type!!area!!built!!Historic Site Status |- |{{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}||Mound length: 120m||Late 5th century||National Historic Site |- |{{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 123m||Early 6th century||National Historic Site |- |{{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 128m||Late 6th century||National Historic Site |- |'''Kabutozuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Mound length: 80m||Late 6th century||None |- |{{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|qq=}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 78.5m||Late 6th century||Prefectural Historic Site |- |{{ill|Sannōzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sannōzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|qq=}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 89m||Late 6th to early 7th century||None |- |{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maruzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|qq=}}||{{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Diameter: 65m||Early 7th century||Prefectural Historic Site |}
Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long [[ja:甲塚古墳 (下野市)]] == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (National) === * Artifacts from Kabutozuka Kofun (archaeological materials) - Specific items include: ** Two loom-shaped Haniwa ** 17 figurative Haniwa ** Four horse-shaped Haniwa ** 58 pieces of Sue pottery ** 16 pieces of Haji pottery ** (Additional) Four fragments of Haniwa Designated on September 15, 2017, and housed at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Omoi River (Tochigi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji Remains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Omoi River (Tochigi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji Remains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}}. It is part of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja|しもつけ古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491515}} (Iizuka-Kokubunji area). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==

Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long [[ja:甲塚古墳 (下野市)]] == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (National) === * Artifacts from Kabutozuka Kofun (archaeological materials) - Specific items include: ** Two loom-shaped Haniwa ** 17 figurative Haniwa ** Four horse-shaped Haniwa ** 58 Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Omoi River (Tochigi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji Remains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Omoi River (Tochigi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji Remains|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (National) === * Artifacts from Kabutozuka Kofun (archaeological materials) - Specific items include: ** Two loom-shaped Haniwa ** 17 figurative Haniwa ** Four horse-shaped Haniwa ** 58 pieces of Sue It is part of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja|しもつけ古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491515}} (Iizuka-Kokubunji area). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==

Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long [[ja:甲塚古墳 (下野市)]] == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} (National) === * Artifacts from Kabutozuka Kofun (archaeological materials) - Specific items include: ** Two loom-shaped Haniwa ** 17 figurative Haniwa ** Four horse-shaped Haniwa ** 58 Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City|1=Shimotsuke, Tochigi}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Q11491515|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubunji ruins|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City|1=Shimotsuke, Tochigi}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Q11491515|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubunji ruins|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==

Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City|1=Shimotsuke, Tochigi}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Q11491515|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubunji ruins|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} located in {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City|1=Shimotsuke, Tochigi}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi Prefecture}}. It is part of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja|しもつけ古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491515|1=Shimotsuke Kofun Group}} (Iizuka-Kokubunji area). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==
{| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%;" |+List of Shimotsuke Kofuns (Iizuka-Kokubunji area) !Mound name!!type!!area!!built!!Historic Site Status |- |{{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}||{{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}||Mound length: 120m||Late 5th century||National Historic Site |- |{{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 123m||Early 6th century||National Historic Site |- |{{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 128m||Late 6th century||National Historic Site |- |'''Kabutozuka Kofun'''||{{ill|Scallop-shaped Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Mound length: 80m||Late 6th century||None |- |{{ill|Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|愛宕塚古墳 (下野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagozuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|qq=}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 78.5m||Late 6th century||Prefectural Historic Site |- |{{ill|Sannōzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|山王塚古墳 (下野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sannōzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|qq=}}||Keyhole-shaped Kofun||Mound length: 89m||Late 6th to early 7th century||None |- |{{ill|Maruzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|ja|丸塚古墳 (下野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maruzuka Kofun (Shimotsuke)|qq=}}||{{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}||Diameter: 65m||Early 7th century||Prefectural Historic Site |}
Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long [[ja:甲塚古墳 (下野市)]] == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City|1=Shimotsuke, Tochigi}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Q11491515|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubunji ruins|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 Kabutozuka Kofun is located on a plateau in western {{ill|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|en|Shimotsuke, Tochigi|WD=Q851804|lt=Shimotsuke City|1=Shimotsuke, Tochigi}}, nestled between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi)|ja|思川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi)|1=Q11491515|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491515}}. The area features a cluster of Kofuns, including notable large-map_size tumuli such as {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. This mound underwent archaeological investigations during 1883 and 1893 (Meiji 16 and 26), which resulted in significant changes to its original condition. The tumulus is characterized as a scallop-shaped keyhole mound with a short anterior mound facing south. It features a two-tiered mound structure, with the first tier having a flat base characteristic of the unique "Shimotsuke-style mounds" of the region. The mound measures approximately 80 meters in length, with the main circular mound measuring 61 meters in diameter. Distinctive finds include rows of cylindrical {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=Haniwa|1=Haniwa}} and decorative Haniwa figures, such as weavers, humans, and horses, notable for their excellent preservation, original positions, and traces of paintHistoric Site Explanation Board.. The burial chamber is a tuff-stone {{ill|Yokoana stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}, opening southward from the anterior mound. The tumulus is dated to the late 6th century. burial goods excavated from the mound were Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} of Japan in 2017. The site lies adjacent to the ruins of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|ja|下野国分寺跡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kokubun-ji|1=Shimotsuke Kokubunji ruins|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11361382}} temple complex. == burial == The burial chamber is constructed from cut tuff stones and is oriented southward from the anterior mound. Although partially destroyed, the chamber's area are estimated as follows: * Total length: 4.2 meters (approximately 9 meters including the burial path). * Main chamber: Length 3.0 meters, Width 2.0 meters, Height 1.9 meters. * Entry passage: Length 0.6 meters. == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (Nationally Designated) === * burial goods excavated from Kabutozuka Kofun, Tochigi Prefecture (archaeological materials). Stored and exhibited at the Shimotsuke Fudoki-no-Oka Museum. Designated on September 15, 2017Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notification No. 117, September 15, 2017.[http://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/2017031002.html Regarding National Treasures and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} designation1] (Agency for Cultural Affairs).{{National designation1 Database|201|00011756|Kabutozuka Kofun burial goods}}. ** Weaving Haniwa figures (2 items). ** Human-shaped Haniwa (17 items). ** Horse-shaped Haniwa (4 items). ** {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} (58 items). ** {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery|1=Haji pottery}} (16 items). ** (Supplementary Historic Site): Haniwa fragments (4 items). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==

Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (National) === * Artifacts from Kabutozuka Kofun (archaeological materials) - Specific items include: ** Two loom-shaped Haniwa ** 17 figurative Haniwa Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi Prefecture}}. It is part of the {{ill|Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja|しもつけ古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Kofuns|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491515|1=Shimotsuke Kofun Group}} (Iizuka-Kokubunji area). Although not designated as a historic site, artifacts from the site have been classified as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}.[http://www.shimotsuke-bunkazai.com/culturalassets.php?id=45 Kabutozuka Kofun] (Shimotsuke City Virtual Cultural Assets Museum). == Overview ==

Located on a plateau between the {{ill|Sugata River|ja|姿川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugata River|1=Sugata River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447636}} and {{ill|Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|ja|思川 (栃木県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omoi River (Tochigi Prefecture)|1=Omoi River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11491516}} in the western area of Shimotsuke City, this Kofun is among several large mounds in the area, including {{ill|Marishitenzuka Kofun|en|Marishitenzuka Kofun|WD=Q17210244|lt=Marishitenzuka Kofun|1=Marishitenzuka Kofun}}, {{ill|Biwazuka Kofun|en|Biwazuka Kofun|WD=Q17230002|lt=Biwazuka Kofun|1=Biwazuka Kofun}}, and {{ill|Azuma Kofun|en|Azuma Kofun|WD=Q17191453|lt=Azuma Kofun|1=Azuma Kofun}}. Excavations were conducted in 1883 and 1893, damaging the original structure. The mound has a short front section, characteristic of scallop-shaped Kofuns, and is oriented south. It is built in two tiers, with the first tier forming a flat pedestal. This is a distinctive feature of "Shimotsuke-style kofun." The mound length is estimated at 80 meters, with the main circular section measuring 61 meters in diameter.Historical site explanation board. Haniwa, including cylindrical and figurative types, have been found on the mound. The site is particularly noted for the discovery of weaving loom-shaped Haniwa, the first of its kind in Japan. Some Haniwa retain traces of original coloring. The burial chamber, constructed of tuff stone, opens to the south from the front section. Estimated reconstructed dimensions of the chamber are as follows: * Total chamber length: 4.2 meters (approx. 9 meters including the burial path) * Main chamber: 3.0 meters long, 2.0 meters wide, 1.9 meters high * Passageway: 0.6 meters long [[ja:甲塚古墳 (下野市)]] == Historic Site == === {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} (National) === * Artifacts from Kabutozuka Kofun (archaeological materials) - Specific items include: ** Two loom-shaped Haniwa ** 17 figurative Haniwa
